note.question: When does dropping a standardized-test requirement broaden access at an acceptable information cost, and how does competition between schools change their incentives to adopt test-optional policies?
note.overview: In the strategic extension, two schools simultaneously decide whether to require test scores, students respond by deciding whether to test and where to apply, and schools set admission thresholds. The paper formally defines equilibrium student applications and school policies and characterizes the resulting policy-game equilibria.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Schools simultaneously announce whether they require the test. Each school observes its applicant information, sets a capacity-constrained threshold, admits students, and admitted students enroll at their preferred school. Dropping tests removes a noisy but informative signal and also removes unequal costs of producing that signal. With one test-requiring school, student testing follows a skill threshold.
